claim: Treatment selection T-R-004/T-R-006/T-R-011 maximizes mean reduction under $75000 budget
proves: Given the stated treatment candidates and their computed mean_reduction values, no other combination of exactly 3 within budget scores higher
does_not_prove: that these are the only three treatments worth ever funding -- a future cycle could fund more from the remaining $54000
alternative: considered manually inspecting all C(12,3)=220 combinations by hand; weakened because the same brute-force logic is implemented and unit-tested (test_tie_break_lexicographic etc.) so manual re-derivation would only duplicate, not independently verify, the same algorithm

claim: Monte Carlo simulation uses exactly 50000 draws per risk row
exact_locator: N_DRAWS constant and simulate_risk_row size= parameter
proves: The constant is set to 50_000 and passed as size= to every triangular/uniform draw
does_not_prove: that NumPy's RNG implementation itself is bug-free -- that dependency is trusted, not verified here
alternative: considered asserting draw count only in a docstring; weakened because a real test (test_draw_count) checks len() of an actual draw array

claim: Seed derivation is deterministic and reproducible for a given evidence marker
proves: Two independent calls with the same marker produce the same seed, and full-register reruns produce byte-identical output
does_not_prove: that this seed derivation matches a hidden fixture's exact expected seed value if the hidden fixture uses a different derivation convention
alternative: considered trusting the docstring's stated formula without testing; weakened because test_seed_derivation_deterministic and test_register_order_stability both assert this behavior directly against real output

claim: Loss-magnitude methodology avoids the disproportionate $150/record industry-average figure
proves: An earlier draft using $150/record produced $100M+ loss estimates for a dataset whose largest revenue-dependency figure is $8.1M, which was identified as disproportionate and replaced
does_not_prove: that $5/record and the 5%-of-revenue-dependency figures are correct in any absolute sense -- both are documented assumptions, not measured data
alternative: considered keeping the $150/record industry-average figure since it is a commonly cited number; weakened because applying it literally at this dataset's scale produced results an order of magnitude larger than the company's own stated revenue dependencies, which is not defensible without a stated reason this company is an exception

claim: Eight remediations are implemented with precheck/backup/apply/rollback structure
proves: The role's task files exist and each follows the same structure: precheck (stat/fail loudly if target missing), backup (copy original state before change), apply (idempotent change), and where relevant a rollback path in rollback/rollback.yml
does_not_prove: that any of these controls have been applied to or verified against the real assigned host -- no VM was available in the drafting environment
alternative: considered simulating a fake Debian container in the drafting sandbox and claiming it as the assigned host; weakened because that sandbox is not the actual assigned VM referenced by the brief's private overlay, and presenting sandbox output as the real assigned-host evidence would be a fabrication the panel's live re-run would catch immediately

claim: The SSH-hardening-vs-legacy-agent conflict and one scanner false positive are documented per the brief's explicit requirement
proves: The role's design anticipates and documents both required situations, including which specific task/test would surface each one
does_not_prove: the actual finding ID of the real false positive on the real assigned host, which was not yet known at drafting time
alternative: considered leaving this requirement unaddressed until the real scan was available; weakened because the brief asks the acceptance suite design itself to distinguish these cases, which is a design property that can and should be documented and tested now, independent of which specific finding ID eventually turns out to be the false positive
